findings.title: Python and Rust used Unicode scalar ordering instead of required UTF-16 key ordering
findings.exploitPreconditions: Content contains object keys whose Unicode scalar order differs from UTF-16 code-unit order, such as U+1F600 and U+E000.
evidence: TypeScript produced {"??":2,"?":1}; Python and Rust produced {"?":1,"??":2} for the same JSON value.
protocol/spec.md:135 and :144 require UTF-16 code-unit comparison.
findings.impact: Conformant-looking implementations could derive different contentHash and blockHash values for identical content.
findings.severityRationale: SECURITY.md classifies defects that can produce incorrect hashes as critical.
reproduction: Replay canonical vector C28 in all three native suites.

remediation.summary: Added canonical vector C28 and UTF-16 sort keys/comparators in Python and Rust.

findings.disposition: Remediated in the Phase 2 worktree; independent retest remains required.
findings.residualRisk: Lone surrogate handling is tracked separately in ALX-ISR-2026-006.

findings.title: Rust number parsing and formatting diverged from JavaScript and unsafe exponent-form integers were inconsistently accepted
findings.trustBoundary: Cross-runtime numeric canonicalization and Block identity
findings.exploitPreconditions: Content contains boundary decimals or numerically integral exponent-form IEEE 754 values.
evidence: Rust rounded 999999.9999999999 and 1000000.0000000001 to 1000000 before float_roundtrip parsing was enabled.
Python and Rust accepted 1e+21 while TypeScript rejected it as an unsafe integral value.
findings.impact: The same JSON number could produce different canonical bytes and therefore different Block identities.
findings.severityRationale: SECURITY.md classifies defects that can produce incorrect hashes as critical.
reproduction: Replay vectors C29-C31 and CN10 in all three native suites.

remediation.summary: Enabled exact serde_json float parsing, expanded scientific notation by decimal-string shifting, and enforced safe range for all integral-valued floats.

findings.disposition: Remediated in the Phase 2 worktree; independent retest remains required.
findings.residualRisk: The deterministic audit samples 5,000 accepted IEEE 754 bit patterns in addition to canonical vectors; independent exhaustive analysis remains pending.

findings.title: TypeScript sparse arrays produced invalid canonical JSON and incorrect Block identity
findings.trustBoundary: JavaScript-native content to serialized Block exchange
findings.exploitPreconditions: A caller creates content with a sparse JavaScript array.
evidence: canonicalizeProtocolJson([1, , 3]) returned [1,,3] while JSON serialization and protocol rules require [1,null,3].
findings.impact: A locally created Block could use non-JSON canonical bytes and fail identity verification after ordinary JSON transport.
findings.severityRationale: SECURITY.md classifies defects that can produce incorrect hashes as critical.
reproduction: Run node --test sdk/src/__tests__/canonicalization.test.js and inspect the sparse-array regression.

remediation.summary: Array.from now visits sparse slots so undefined slots canonicalize to null.
regression: sdk/src/__tests__/canonicalization.test.js: undefined and sparse array slots canonicalize to null

findings.disposition: Remediated in the Phase 2 worktree; independent retest remains required.
findings.residualRisk: Non-JSON host objects remain outside the portable vector representation and require in-language coverage.

findings.title: Block validators accepted non-canonical stored blockHash and contentHash encodings
findings.exploitPreconditions: A received Block stores correct digest bytes using uppercase hexadecimal or surrounding whitespace.
evidence: All three validators returned ok:true after normalizing uppercase or whitespace-padded stored identity fields, despite protocol/spec.md:167 requiring exact lowercase format.
findings.impact: Structurally invalid Block representations bypassed the public semantic verifier and could be admitted by callers that rely on validateBlock alone.
findings.severityRationale: SECURITY.md classifies verification bypass as critical.
reproduction: Replay semantic-validity vectors SV7 and SV8 in all three conformance suites.

remediation.summary: Validators still normalize for diagnostic compatibility but now require each stored identity field to equal its normalized form before ok can be true.

findings.disposition: Remediated in the Phase 2 worktree; independent retest remains required.
findings.residualRisk: Callers must continue to treat thrown malformed-hash errors as validation failure.

findings.title: Public recursion state allowed depth-limit bypass and TypeScript rejected reused non-cyclic objects
findings.exploitPreconditions: A caller supplies undocumented recursion parameters or reuses an object reference in separate branches.
evidence: canonicalizeProtocolJson(value, -10) accepted content that the normal call rejected above depth 128.
The TypeScript WeakSet retained completed child objects and reported a cycle for {a: shared, b: shared}.
findings.impact: The depth control could be bypassed, increasing stack-exhaustion risk, while valid JSON-compatible inputs could be rejected inconsistently.
findings.severityRationale: The repository rubric classifies denial-of-service and resource-limit defects as medium.

remediation.summary: Recursion state is private in TypeScript and Python, and TypeScript removes completed objects from the active ancestor set.

findings.residualRisk: The fixed recursive design still relies on the specified maximum depth rather than an iterative serializer.

findings.title: Lone UTF-16 surrogate acceptance is not interoperably defined

affected.symbol: canonical string and JSON-serializable content rules

findings.trustBoundary: Cross-language parsing and canonicalization of escaped string data
findings.exploitPreconditions: Content or an object key contains an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escape such as \ud800.
evidence: TypeScript canonicalized an unpaired surrogate as an escaped code unit.
Python accepted the value in memory but failed UTF-8 encoding during Block hashing or adapter output.
serde_json rejected the JSON input because Rust String requires valid Unicode scalar values.
findings.impact: A JavaScript producer can accept content that Python and Rust cannot hash or exchange, causing deterministic interoperability failure.
findings.severityRationale: The defect causes targeted cross-runtime denial of service without demonstrating hash forgery.
reproduction: Send {"operation":"canonicalize","input":"\ud800"} to each conformance adapter and compare acceptance.

remediation.summary: Protocol decision required: either reject unpaired surrogates in every runtime or define a code-unit-preserving portable representation.

findings.disposition: Open; changing acceptance semantics requires an approved canonical protocol decision and vectors.
findings.residualRisk: JavaScript callers must avoid unpaired surrogate content until the protocol policy is resolved.
